description:
What is Lama Chopa?

Lama Chopa, also known as the Guru Puja, is a guru yoga text composed by Panchen Losang Chökyi Gyaltsen. FPMT centers commonly perform it as a group practice on the 10th and 25th days of the

Tibetan lunar calendar. Anyone may join the puja itself, but study of the practice and its commentaries is reserved for those who have received the highest yoga tantra initiation.

According to Lama Zopa Rinpoche's commentary on the practice, Lama Chopa holds a special place among guru yoga texts for several reasons: it carries the full lamrim (stages of the path) prayer, which plants the imprint of the entire path to enlightenment in the mind; it contains specific Mahayana thought- transformation instructions for turning any experience, pleasant or difficult, into a cause of happiness for all beings; and it brings together the three main highest yoga tantra deities — Guhyasamaja, Chakrasamvara, and Yamantaka — within a single practice.

Rinpoche has also explained that at its heart, Lama Chopa simply means pleasing the guru — so in daily life, any action done to please the holy mind of one's teachers can itself be considered guru puja.
